headline: Attackers turned a JavaScript-security vendor's own npm package into an infostealer and abused GitHub's API for mass reconnaissance, driving home that the developer supply chain is the day's battleground.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep bending developer infrastructure to their ends, poisoning the jscrambler npm package to drop a native infostealer while throwaway accounts quietly map GitHub organizations for their next round of targets.
Artificial intelligence now cuts both ways in vulnerability research, this week unearthing a root-privilege bug in the Linux kernel that human reviewers walked past for fifteen years.
Foundational open-source software carries decades-old wounds, from the 29-year-old Squidbleed flaw that leaks HTTP requests to a fresh batch of twelve fixes in Wireshark.

topics.title: Compromised jscrambler npm Package
topics.latest_developments: Attackers pushed a malicious jscrambler 8.14.0 release to npm on July 11, 2026, whose preinstall hook drops and runs a native Rust infostealer compiled for Windows, macOS, and Linux, and Socket flagged the version six minutes after publication.
topics.summary: Jscrambler builds JavaScript obfuscation and protection tools, so anyone who installed version 8.14.0 ran the infostealer automatically. Roll the package back, rotate any credentials the build touched, and hunt for the dropped binary.

sources.title: Compromised jscrambler 8.14.0 npm Release Drops Rust Infostealer During Install

topics.title: Ghost Accounts Map GitHub Organizations
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported July 11, 2026 that multiple campaigns spin up disposable ghost accounts to abuse the GitHub API and enumerate organizations' repositories and members at scale.
topics.summary: The reconnaissance profiles GitHub organizations, likely to seed later targeted attacks against developers and their code. Restrict API exposure and watch for anomalous enumeration of members and repos.

sources.title: Ghost Accounts Abuse GitHub API in Mass Recon Campaign

topics.title: Espionage Against Pakistani Police
topics.latest_developments: Researchers disclosed July 11, 2026 that suspected China- and India-aligned actors ran sustained espionage against Pakistani law enforcement from February 2024 through April 2026, compromising Balochistan Police servers that host web applications managing criminal and citizen records.
topics.summary: The intrusions struck several Pakistani law enforcement organizations and exposed police and citizen data across multiple espionage campaigns. Affected agencies should hunt for the compromise and lock down internet-facing web applications.

sources.title: Hackers Weaponize Balochistan Police Portal in Multi-Group Espionage Campaigns

topics.title: AI Uncovers 15-Year-Old Linux Root Bug
topics.latest_developments: Wired reported July 11, 2026 that an AI system found a root-privilege bug in the Linux kernel that human reviewers overlooked for fifteen years.
topics.summary: AI-driven code analysis is surfacing long-buried kernel flaws that grant local root access. Administrators should track the forthcoming fix and update their kernels promptly.

sources.title: AI Found a Root Bug in Linux That Everyone Missed for 15 Years

topics.title: Wireshark 4.6.7 Patches
topics.latest_developments: The Wireshark project shipped version 4.6.7 on July 11, 2026, fixing 12 vulnerabilities and 16 bugs.
topics.summary: Wireshark is the standard network-protocol analyzer, and malformed captures can crash or exploit older builds. Update to 4.6.7.

topics.title: Squidbleed Squid Proxy Flaw
topics.latest_developments: Bruce Schneier flagged July 10, 2026 a 29-year-old bug in the Squid proxy, dubbed Squidbleed, that can leak the contents of HTTP requests.
topics.summary: Squid is a widely deployed open-source caching proxy, and the flaw can expose sensitive request data to attackers. Operators should apply the fixed release.

business_politics.title: Iran Hormuz Deadline Passes, Nuclear Talks Falter
business_politics.latest_developments: The Saturday, July 11, deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz arrived as the Trump administration signaled it now doubts any nuclear deal, and Trump and Iran's leadership traded fresh threats after Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's funeral.
business_politics.summary: A senior U.S. official demanded Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz—the chokepoint carrying roughly a fifth of the world's crude—or face consequences, while mediators scrambled to salvage a crumbling agreement as the Trump administration grew pessimistic about reaching a nuclear accord with Tehran.

sources.title: Trump Administration Increasingly Pessimistic of Clinching Iran Nuclear Deal
Inside the risky race through the Strait of Hormuz

business.title: Western Pennsylvania's Tipping Fatigue
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported July 11 on a growing local backlash against gratuity prompts.
business.summary: TribLive found Western Pennsylvania consumers pushing back as more businesses add tip suggestions and gratuity requests to checkout screens, testing where shoppers draw the line on prompted tipping.

sources.title: Western Pennsylvanians react to growing tipping culture, gratuity requests

around_teams.title: Pirates' Use of Mlodzinski Questioned
around_teams.latest_developments: In a July 11 column, Post-Gazette writer Noah Hiles argued the Pirates must make better use of reliever Carmen Mlodzinski.
around_teams.summary: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles wrote that manager Don Kelly and general manager Ben Cherington are underusing right-handed reliever Carmen Mlodzinski as the Pittsburgh Pirates work through bullpen struggles and mounting injuries.

team_usa.title: America Embraces Its Home World Cup
team_usa.latest_developments: The Guardian reported July 11 on how the tournament captivated the United States even after the men's team's exit.
team_usa.summary: The Guardian described packed stadiums and record television audiences as the United States embraced hosting the 2026 World Cup, framing the tournament as a unifying, multicultural celebration that arrived despite President Trump's threats against co-hosts Canada and Mexico and his tightened travel restrictions.

sources.title: 'A brilliant reprieve, a unifying force': America falls in love with World Cup
